instructions: Complete the summary using the list of words and phrases, A-J, below.
stem_block:
Peer effects in a company with no offices

Caster Inc has never run a physical office, which makes it an unusually clean setting in which to study how colleagues shape one another's output. New staff were sorted into teams purely by the order in which they arrived, a rule neither managers nor employees could bend, so team make-up amounted in practice to (36) ........ , and the authors could argue for cause rather than mere association. Output was recorded as the number of clients a person looked after in a month, a figure that standard hours and fixed contracts turn into (37) ........ of how much useful work was really done. Being placed beside the company's strongest performers brought (38) ........ , even in the most productive quarter of teams. What counted instead was (39) ........ : teams whose members had stayed longest raised the output of those around them, and the gain was largest for staff still in their first year. Since the most experienced teams in fact exchanged fewer messages than the rest, the authors conclude that such groups rely on a shared, unspoken sense of who knows what, and that steady contact is largely (40) ........ for people who already know their job.

items.prompt: New staff were sorted into teams purely by the order in which they arrived, a rule neither managers nor employees could bend, so team make-up amounted in practice to (36) ........ , and the authors could argue for cause rather than mere association.
items.evidence: This effectively randomised which colleagues an employee ended up working alongside, letting the researchers treat team composition almost as if it had been assigned in a controlled experiment, and so identify cause and effect rather than mere correlation.
items.explanation: Paragraph C says that assigning staff by order of arrival made team composition effectively random, letting the researchers treat it almost like a controlled experiment; the correct answer is therefore A ('a controlled experiment').
items.flag_reason: Cevap A ('a controlled experiment'), arastirma yontemi mantigiyla kelime bankasi icinde tek tutarli secenek: sira ile rastgele atama, deneysel kontrollu bir duzenlemeye esdeger sayilir -- bu standart arastirma yontemi kavramiyla parcaya bakmadan da secilebiliyor.

items.prompt: Output was recorded as the number of clients a person looked after in a month, a figure that standard hours and fixed contracts turn into (37) ........ of how much useful work was really done.
items.evidence: Because the company standardises working hours and each client contract allocates a fixed thirty hours of monthly support, the number of clients handled is a dependable stand-in for how much useful work an individual completed, avoiding the ambiguity that self-reported effort or hours worked can introduce into workplace research.
items.explanation: Paragraph D says that, thanks to standardised working hours and the fixed thirty hours in each contract, the number of clients is a 'reliable' measure of work done; the correct answer is therefore C. Option D ('a rough guide') is wrong, because the text stresses that this measure avoids ambiguity.
items.flag_reason: Cevap C ('a reliable measure'), kelime bankasindaki en yakin celdirici D ('a rough guide' -- kabaca bir kilavuz) ile karsit; metindeki 'guvenilir' vurgusu D'nin tahmini/kaba tonuyla celisiyor, bu yuzden yalniz C metinle ortusuyor.

items.prompt: Being placed beside the company's strongest performers brought (38) ........ , even in the most productive quarter of teams.
items.evidence: Working alongside colleagues who were themselves highly productive produced no measurable improvement in an individual's own output, even for employees placed in teams whose average productivity ranked in the top quarter of the company.
items.explanation: Paragraph E says that working alongside highly productive colleagues produced no measurable improvement in a person's own output, even in the top-quarter teams; the correct answer is therefore I.
items.flag_reason: Cevap I ('no measurable benefit'), kelime bankasindaki en yakin celdirici B ('a distraction') ile karistirilabilir, ama metin burada dikkat dagitmadan degil dogrudan bir fayda yoklugundan soz ediyor; 'en verimli ceyrekte bile' ifadesi yalniz I ile ortusuyor.

items.prompt: What counted instead was (39) ........ : teams whose members had stayed longest raised the output of those around them, and the gain was largest for staff still in their first year.
items.evidence: Employees placed in teams with the most experienced average tenure, the top twenty-five per cent of teams by this measure, saw their own productivity rise by roughly 12.2 per cent.
items.explanation: Paragraph F says that the deciding factor was not raw productivity but a team's average tenure, and that output rose by about 12.2% for staff in the highest-tenure teams; since tenure means length of service, the correct answer is H.
items.flag_reason: Cevap H ('length of service'), metindeki 'ortalama kidem' (tenure) kavraminin dogrudan es anlamlisi; kelime bankasindaki digerleri (egitim suresi, sosyal kiyas, yuz yuze temas) bu kavrami karsilamiyor.

items.prompt: Since the most experienced teams in fact exchanged fewer messages than the rest, the authors conclude that such groups rely on a shared, unspoken sense of who knows what, and that steady contact is largely (40) ........ for people who already know their job.
items.evidence: In fact, teams with the highest average tenure communicated internally less than other teams, a statistically significant difference, and experienced or already highly productive employees tended to perform best in exactly these lower-communication settings, suggesting that frequent messaging may sometimes distract rather than assist workers who already know what they are doing.
items.explanation: Paragraph G says that frequent messaging may distract, rather than help, staff who already know their job; the correct answer is therefore B ('a distraction').
items.flag_reason: Cevap B ('a distraction'), metindeki 'may sometimes distract rather than assist' ifadesinin dogrudan karsiligi; kelime bankasindaki oteki secenekler (guvenilir olcum, kontrollu deney, sosyal kiyas) bu baglama uymuyor.
